newsitem.title: USA: Calif. legislature to consider flood relief.
newsitem.headline: Calif. legislature to consider flood relief.

text.p: A special session of the California state legislature was set to get underway on Tuesday to consider measures to aid the victims of recent flooding and help counties cope with the damage.
The session had been expected to begin on Monday but its start was delayed due to scheduling conflicts, state officials said.
The special session was now expected to convene Tuesday afternoon in the state Assembly. The state Senate will meet in special session on Friday, officials said.

Once the special session gets underway, several state lawmakers said they planned to introduce proposals to aid victims of the floods and hard-hit local governments. A special session waives certain rules, allowing the legislature to act more quickly on relief proposals.

Damage estimates from the devastating New Year floods have passed $1.5 billion. Officials said the floods were almost certain to be the most costly in state history, surpassing the $1.8 billion of losses suffered in severe 1995 floods.
